item.title: They Will See Johnny's Message: A Measurement Study of Post-Quantum Cryptography Across Email Delivery Paths
item.description: Harvest-now, decrypt-later (HNDL) attacks make the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) urgent for email. This paper presents a systematic measurement that jointly examines PQC deployment across email service stages, negotiation by communicating peers, and usable message encryption.

item.title: RoboAuto: Autonomous Robot Program Search through Multi-Level Physical Understanding
item.description: Recently, LLM-based autonomous agents have shown strong capabilities in iteratively generating, evaluating, and refining executable solutions. In robotic manipulation, Code-as-Policy lets these agents search over modular and editable robot programs.

item.description: Large language model (LLM) agents are extending agent-mediated commerce on the Web from shopping for consumers to operating businesses for sellers. In online-to-offline (O2O) commerce, decisions are issued through Web-based platforms but realized through costly physical execution.

item.title: Learning Multi-Phase Robot Loco-Manipulation via Phase-Conditioned Policy Optimization
item.description: Complex whole-body loco-manipulation requires executing diverse maneuvers, such as crouching, grasping, and locomotion, within a single long-horizon task. item.title: AlphaCNOT: Learning CNOT Minimization with Model-Based Planning
item.description: Quantum circuit optimization is a central task in quantum computing, as current NISQ devices suffer from error propagation that often scales with the number of operations. Among quantum operations, the CNOT gate is of fundamental importance, being the only two-qubit gate in the universal Clifford+T set.

item.title: MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Agent memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to reuse past experiences without updating their parameters. However, semantic similarity alone does not guarantee memory usefulness: downstream performance depends on how memories are selected and presented to the agent.

item.title: Designing Quantum Solutions to the Closest String Problem with the Non-Variational QWOA
item.description: Quantum computing offers promising approaches to combinatorial optimization problems whose search spaces grow exponentially with problem size. The Closest String problem belongs to this category, which seeks a string that minimizes the maximum Hamming distance to any string in a given collection of reference strings.

item.title: Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians
item.description: Simulation of molecular vibrations is emerging as a promising application of quantum computing in quantum chemistry. item.title: Feasibility of Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing: From Quantum Links to Algorithms
item.description: Practical fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a large number of physical qubits, posing a major challenge for scaling up individual quantum processors. Distributed architectures offer a promising solution by interconnecting multiple processors through quantum networks.

item.title: Minimal ancilla for boosting type-I photonic fusion
item.description: Fusion gates enable the creation of large entangled photonic states for linear-optical quantum computing and communication protocols. However, their success probability is limited to $1/2$ without additional photonic resources.

item.title: Quantum computation of energy level degeneracy and thermodynamical properties of spin systems
item.description: We propose a hybrid quantum-classical method for reconstructing energy-level degeneracies and thermodynamic properties of spin systems. A single ancilla qubit is used to measure the partition function at imaginary inverse temperatures.
